with_skill.expectation: Calls out that testing with real card numbers must stop, treating it as a compliance/terms violation rather than a mere inconvenience.
Treats 'every vendor publishes a distinct sandbox throttle' as false, noting sandbox-specific numeric limits are sparsely documented across vendors and several reuse production limits.
Keeps leaked-key mitigations distinct: server-side-only secrets, scoped/restricted keys, and secret-scanning enrollment.
Notes test keys are not risk-free - on a toggle model they still read and write real account configuration - so they deserve real secret hygiene.

without_skill.expectation: Requires each magic value to map onto a real published error/decline code from the API's error catalog, never a sandbox-only error shape.
States the sandbox's isolation level explicitly in the docs instead of letting the word 'sandbox' imply it.
Notes that graduation to live will be gated by a compliance step (KYC-style activation) and recommends integrators submit it early because review can take days.
States the asymmetry that adding new magic values is safe while changing or removing existing ones is a breaking change.
Identifies the unlabeled multi-operation catalog as a documented integrator trap (cross-referencing the wrong operation's meaning).
Recommends bidirectional mode-boundary enforcement: live credentials reject magic numbers and test credentials reject real ones.
States the sandbox's isolation level explicitly in documentation instead of relying on the word 'sandbox'.
Applies the event/time coverage gate: every time-dependent flow must be testable via simulated time, and any flow testable only by waiting real calendar time fails the audit.
Mentions auto-aging fixtures (date fields shifting daily) as a cheaper rung for simple cases, distinct from the full clock primitive.
Recommends reset endpoints that return a developer's test environment to a clean state.
Recommends deriving sandbox configuration from the same infrastructure-as-code as production so any difference is intentional and documented.
Promotes the config-driven fixture builder because integrators' data shapes genuinely vary, naming the data-aggregation domain as the promotion condition.
States the shared sandbox's isolation level explicitly in docs - shared and not per-integrator isolated - instead of letting 'sandbox' imply isolation.
Applies the failure-path coverage gate: every documented failure outcome deterministically triggerable, with a single untriggerable path failing the audit.
Requires the environment boundary to prevent test credentials from referencing or touching real accounts.
Cites the quantified precedent that managed CAPTCHA on checkout cut card testing by about 80% with under 0.02% impact on authorization rates.
Rejects the 10 requests/minute sandbox limiter as the default and recommends reusing production rate limits unchanged in the sandbox as the default posture.
Gives the reason for limit parity: identical limits keep integrators' throttling and backoff code honest before they hit production.
Treats 'every vendor publishes a distinct sandbox throttle' as false, noting sandbox-specific numeric limits are sparsely documented across vendors and several reuse production limits.
Keeps leaked-key mitigations distinct: server-side-only secrets, scoped/restricted keys, and secret-scanning enrollment.
Notes test keys are not risk-free - on a toggle model they still read and write real account configuration - so they deserve real secret hygiene.
Requires test credentials removed from production configuration, not merely live credentials added.
Names the cross-environment paste pitfall (live key in a sandbox context or vice versa) and its opaque authentication-failure symptom as a recurring support generator.
Includes a reactive go-back trigger: webhooks silently stopping after launch usually means a stale or unregistered live-mode endpoint from a silently skipped cutover step.
Names the drift failure mode: when the API changes, the mock keeps simulating the old behavior while production breaks silently, which vendor-exercised real objects cannot do.
States that the bugs a stateless mock misses are the state-dependent ones surfacing weeks into an integration, not day-one request-shape errors.
Recommends building a real stateful test mode instead, with the soft toggle named as the default isolation rung.
Requires the docs to state the isolation level explicitly rather than shipping the bare label 'Sandbox'.
Applies the failure-path coverage gate at 100%, with one untriggerable failure path failing the audit.
Specifies mode-prefixed test credentials with the recognized _test_/_live_ substring shape for the real test mode, rather than reusing live keys against a different host.
Explains why test keys carry risk: on a toggle model they still read and write real account configuration, and the prefix communicates mode, not risk level.
Frames the wrong-environment paste as a named recurring support-ticket generator with a design target of zero cross-environment incidents, achieved structurally rather than by warning developers.
Requires bidirectional boundary enforcement: live keys reject test data and test keys reject real records.
